claim.summary: Guarded opt-in dense BF16 load/SIMD reduction accelerates measured backbone projections while preserving tested native Float32 bits and GPU scheduling.
claim.scope: M2 Max/macOS 26.6.2, pinned checkpoint, actual layer-0 shapes and three real normalized inputs; exact native full backbone and one short full-generation workload. No default promotion or universal process-speedup claim.

promotion.next_falsifier: Exact row1/layer39 router logits, expert IDs/order, weighted expert outputs and partial sums on one shared normalized input; preserve tolerances.

boundaries.rollback: Keep/unset DRAMA3_BACKBONE_DENSE_REDUCTION=tree; generic dense defaults tree. Revert atomic experiment commit to remove opt-in path.
invariants: No quantization/precision change; baseline dense kernel untouched.
Same per-lane product/add loop and 64-lane tree, FP contraction disabled.
Aligned BF16 loads require even mapped offsets; other dtype/offset paths use original decoder.
Existing device buffers, mapped owners, queue, control and terminal boundaries preserved.
No new intermediate submissions/waits/readbacks, copies or scratch lifetimes.
15 percent sampled reserve; unrelated processes untouched.
excluded: Authenticated artifacts or full weight-shard hashes

implementation: Aligned 16-bit BF16 load plus SIMD shuffle tree behind independent frozen selectors; actual selectors emitted in generation metadata.

upstream.limitations: F32 replay promotes floating checkpoint tensors exactly, preserving packed integers. Whole checkpoint shards were not hashed; selected layer0 projection tensors were hashed. Full parity fails at the same coordinate for both native reductions. Expert-order root cause remains a hypothesis.
